summary: Iter33 — Instant-execution roadmap step #3: auto-create REAL calendar events from AI-detected meetings. FULL PASS backend + frontend. BACKEND (pytest, 5/5 pass in 12.41s, /app/backend/tests/test_iteration33.py): (1) owner login → JWT. (2) 'Arrange a sales review meeting this Friday with the sales team, and set up a vendor call next Monday.' directive → note.status=done in ~10s; execution_summary.meetings=2 (all 6 keys present as ints); decision_id set and mirrored on decisions collection; /api/calendar?days=45 counts.meeting=2 with two new type='meeting' events (Sales Review Meeting with Sales Team → 2026-07-11, Vendor Call → 2026-07-14), both future dates parseable as YYYY-MM-DD within window, non-empty titles, not overdue. source='meeting' to-do tasks created with due_date=null (correctly avoiding calendar 'task' duplication) and decision_id=None. (3) 'Priya, follow up with the Bangalore retailer today.' non-meeting directive → execution_summary.meetings=0 and zero new calendar meeting events. (4) execution_summary shape regression: all 6 keys are ints on every note (tasks, assignees, approvals, workflows, meetings, reminders). (5) Date resolver semantics verified indirectly: resolved dates are strictly >= today and within the 45-day window. FRONTEND (Playwright, all assertions pass): (a) Business Calendar (/calendar) filter chip [data-testid=cal-filter-meeting] is the FIRST TYPE chip (order: cal-filter-all → cal-filter-meeting → payment_due → task → delivery → complaint → birthday), labeled 'Meetings' with count. (b) Submitting the sales-review directive on Decision Desk revealed [data-testid=execution-summary-panel], [data-testid=es-chip-meetings] text='2meetings scheduled' (contains 'scheduled', NOT 'detected'), [data-testid=es-count-meetings]=2. Screenshots confirm dark tile with people icon (UsersThree, bg-brand-ink) for meeting events. (c) After submission, calendar chip updated to 'MEETINGS (2)'; clicking [data-testid=cal-filter-meeting] filtered to show both meeting event cards. CLEANUP: pytest fixture + explicit UI-cleanup script wiped all test-created data (2 voice_notes, 2 decisions, ~4-5 tasks, 4 calendar_events); post-cleanup /api/calendar counts show only baseline {task:82, complaint:1} with no 'meeting' entries.
action_items: (Carried from iter31/32) Add DELETE endpoints for /api/voice-notes/{id}, /api/decisions/{id}, /api/workflows/{id}, and /api/calendar-events/{id} (owner-scoped, with cascade). Current testing agents must fall back to direct mongo access; brittle and error-prone. Two cleanup fixtures now depend on stripping quotes from /app/backend/.env values.

(Nice-to-have) _resolve_meeting_date prefers `due_in_days` (int) over the weekday-name parse of `when`. When the LLM returns due_in_days=3 for 'this Friday' on a Wednesday, the resolved date lands on Saturday (2026-07-11) instead of Friday (2026-07-10) — the calendar subtitle 'THIS FRIDAY' then appears on a Saturday date. Consider a hybrid: when both `when` and `due_in_days` are present and `when` contains a weekday name, prefer the weekday-name path; use `due_in_days` only as a fallback. Not a bug per spec (dates are still future and plausible) but the UX subtitle currently mismatches the day of week.

(Nice-to-have) Add a sidebar NAV entry for '/calendar' (Business Calendar). Currently the Layout.js NAV array has Decision Desk, CEO Brief, My Work, People, Company Brain, Capture, Workflows, Meeting Notes — no direct link to Business Calendar. Users must know the URL. 'Meeting Notes' (/meetings) is a different route (voice-recorded meeting notes), so users conflate them.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:661-679 _resolve_meeting_date — clean helper, well-scoped. Weekday map + 'today/tomorrow/next weekday/next week' branches are covered. `ahead = (idx - now.weekday()) % 7 or 7` correctly avoids returning today for the same weekday (returns +7 instead). 'next <weekday>' adds another 7 days (correct). Default fallback is +2 days.

server.py:664 — if due_in_days is provided as int by the LLM, the resolver skips the weekday-name path entirely. This is the source of the 'this Friday' → Saturday drift noted above. Recommend: `if isinstance(due_in_days, int) and not any(name in (when or '').lower() for name in _WEEKDAYS): return ...` so weekday hints in `when` beat the LLM's due_in_days heuristic.

server.py:766-783 process_voice_note meeting materialization: (a) inserts db.calendar_events with tenant_id, date, title, when_text, decision_id, source='voice', created_by, created_at — comprehensive; (b) also inserts a source='meeting' task with due_date=null, decision_id=None (correctly undated so it does NOT hit the 'task' calendar entry aggregator on server.py:3237). LGTM.

server.py:818 execution_summary.meetings = len(meetings) counts extracted meeting_events (not the DB inserts). If insert ever fails mid-loop, meetings count could over-report vs actual DB state. Minor. Consider incrementing a counter inside the loop instead.

server.py:3269-3272 business_calendar meeting aggregator: `mevs = db.calendar_events.find(...)` and `add(ev.get('date'), 'meeting', ev.get('title', 'Meeting'), ev.get('when_text', ''), None, ev.get('id'))`. Passes when_text as subtitle — the 'THIS FRIDAY' label rendered on Sat Jul 11 in the UI is from this field. contact_id is hardcoded to None (correct — meeting events aren't tied to a contact today; future improvement).

Calendar.js:10-17 TYPES order = { meeting, payment_due, task, delivery, complaint, birthday }. Meetings correctly listed FIRST as required. Icon = UsersThree (bg-brand-ink dark tile) matches spec ('icon = people/UsersThree, dark tile').

ExecutionSummary.js:33 meetings chip label 'meeting scheduled'/'meetings scheduled' matches roadmap step #3 requirement exactly ('scheduled' not 'detected'). Chip color bg-brand-ink is the same dark tile as calendar meeting events — visual consistency across surfaces.

server.py has no DELETE for calendar_events (in addition to still-missing workflows/decisions/voice_notes DELETEs). Testing agents keep polluting the demo tenant on failure paths. Repeated action item since iter31.

Calendar.js:32-35 queryKey ['calendar'] — no invalidation hook exists in the codebase that invalidates ['calendar'] after a voice-note submission. Verified UI still updated because the user navigated away+back, forcing a refetch. Consider invalidating ['calendar'] alongside ['dashboard'] in the voice-note submit mutation (currently invalidates only tasks/decisions/workflows/inbox) so users see the new meeting immediately if they land on Calendar without a full nav.

Rerun backend: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration33.py -o addopts= -v` (~13s, hits Emergent Claude — non-deterministic but assertions are threshold-based and match by title prefix). Playwright selectors verified: [data-testid=text-directive-input], [data-testid=submit-text-directive], [data-testid=clarify-skip], [data-testid=execution-summary-panel], [data-testid=es-chip-meetings], [data-testid=es-count-meetings], [data-testid=es-close-btn], [data-testid=cal-filter-all], [data-testid=cal-filter-meeting], [data-testid=cal-filter-{type}] for each type, [data-testid=cal-day-{date}], [data-testid=cal-event-meeting-{i}], [data-testid=calendar-days]. LLM date drift note: 'this Friday' can resolve to Sat and 'next Monday' can resolve to Tue depending on due_in_days it returned — this is not a bug; the spec accepts any future YYYY-MM-DD.
rca of the issue: No bugs. Feature works end-to-end per roadmap step #3 spec: meeting_events extracted by AI now become real calendar_events (via db.calendar_events collection) with resolved future YYYY-MM-DD dates, execution_summary.meetings counts them, /api/calendar aggregator emits them as type='meeting' entries with the UsersThree icon on a dark tile, the ExecutionSummary chip reads 'meeting(s) scheduled' (not 'detected'), and each meeting is mirrored as a source='meeting' undated to-do task without duplicating on the calendar. Test file test_iteration33.py had one initial failure caused by picking up a pre-seeded source='meeting' task with a due_date — fixed by scoping the meeting-task assertion to tasks whose title matches the newly-created meeting titles (title prefix match). No production code changes were needed.
